text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests evaluated by a healthcare professional.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests evaluated by a healthcare professional

text_blocks.snippet: According to guidelines from organizations like the American Diabetes Association and the Mayo Clinic, doctors use three primary blood tests to confirm a diagnosis:

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar level over the past three months. No fasting is required.
Diabetes: 6.5% or higher (typically confirmed by a repeat test on a second day)
Diabetes: 6.5% or higher (typically confirmed by a repeat test on a second day)
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you do not eat or drink anything except water for at least eight hours.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures blood sugar at any time of day when you have severe symptoms of high blood sugar.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures blood sugar before and two hours after you drink a special sugary liquid.
Diabetes: 200 mg/dL or higher at the two-hour mark
